items.stem: What is meant by mirror or light source?
items.answer: The part that directs light through the specimen
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Mirror or light source – the part that directs light through the specimen.

items.stem: Write the steps to prepare a temporary slide of onion peel.
items.answer: Peel a thin transparent layer from the inner side of an onion scale; place it in a drop of water on a slide; add a drop of safranin/iodine; remove extra stain; add a drop of glycerine; lower a coverslip gently with a needle; observe under low then high power.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each for thin peel, water drop, stain, glycerine, coverslip without bubbles, low-power first (max 3).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Glycerine is added to a slide preparation.
Reason (R): Glycerine stains the nucleus dark blue.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A true (prevents drying); R false.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A cell appears 20 mm long when seen through a microscope with a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective. What is its actual length?
items.markingKey: Magnification = 10 × 40 = 400. Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 20 ÷ 400 = 0.05 mm.

items.stem: A cell appears 10 mm long when seen through a microscope with a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective. What is its actual length?
items.markingKey: Magnification = 10 × 40 = 400. Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 10 ÷ 400 = 0.025 mm.

items.stem: A cell appears 3.75 mm long when seen through a microscope with a 15× eyepiece and a 10× objective. What is its actual length?
items.markingKey: Magnification = 15 × 10 = 150. Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 3.75 ÷ 150 = 0.025 mm.

items.stem: Tara uses a microscope with a 5× eyepiece and a 4× objective lens. What is the total magnification?
items.markingKey: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 5 × 4 = 20×.

items.stem: Write the steps to prepare a temporary slide of human cheek cells.
items.answer: Rinse mouth; gently scrape the inner cheek with a clean toothpick; spread the scraping in a drop of water on a slide; add a drop of methylene blue; add glycerine; place a coverslip at an angle; observe under the microscope.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each step (max 3).

items.stem: Define a vacuole.
items.answer: A space in the cytoplasm filled with cell sap; it is large in plant cells
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A vacuole – a space in the cytoplasm filled with cell sap; it is large in plant cells.

items.stem: Which of the following is found in both plant and animal cells?
items.answer: mitochondria
items.markingKey: (b) Mitochondria is found in both plant and animal cells. The others: chloroplasts – found in plant cells but not in animal cells; a large central vacuole – found in plant cells but not in animal cells; cell wall – found in plant cells but not in animal cells.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Cheek cells contain chloroplasts.
Reason (R): Animal cells do not make their own food.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Classify the following into a unicellular organism and a multicellular organism: mango tree, earthworm, bacteria, Amoeba, Euglena.
items.answer: A unicellular organism: Amoeba, Euglena, bacteria. A multicellular organism: earthworm, mango tree.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A unicellular organism: Amoeba, Euglena, bacteria. A multicellular organism: earthworm, mango tree.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a unicellular organism?
items.answer: frog
items.markingKey: (d) Frog is a multicellular organism, not a unicellular organism. Each of the others (Euglena, bacteria, yeast) is a unicellular organism.

items.stem: Give three differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
items.answer: Plant cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole; animal cell has no cell wall, no chloroplasts and small or no vacuoles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct difference (max 3).

items.stem:
Read: Zoya observed two slides. Slide X showed brick-shaped cells with thick boundaries and many green bodies. Slide Y showed irregular flat cells with a darkly stained centre and thin boundaries.
(i) Which slide is from a leaf? (ii) Name the green bodies. (iii) Which part made the boundary thick in X? (iv) Which stain could she have used for Y?
items.answer: (i) Slide X. (ii) Chloroplasts. (iii) Cell wall. (iv) Methylene blue (Y is cheek cells).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Why is the cell called the basic unit of life?
items.answer: All living things are made of cells, and all life activities such as nutrition, respiration and growth take place in cells.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: all organisms made of cells. 1 mark: functions occur in cells.

items.stem: Which of the following is a unicellular organism?
items.answer: Paramecium
items.markingKey: (d) Paramecium is a unicellular organism. The others: mango tree – a multicellular organism; mushroom – a multicellular organism; human being – a multicellular organism.

items.stem: Classify the following into a unicellular organism and a multicellular organism: mango tree, earthworm, yeast, bacteria, Paramecium.
items.answer: A unicellular organism: Paramecium, bacteria, yeast. A multicellular organism: earthworm, mango tree.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A unicellular organism: Paramecium, bacteria, yeast. A multicellular organism: earthworm, mango tree.

items.stem: Which group of microbes is considered to lie on the boundary between living and non-living?
items.answer: Viruses
items.markingKey: (b) Viruses show life only inside host cells.

items.stem: Which of the following is a protozoan?
items.answer: Amoeba
items.markingKey: (c) Amoeba is a protozoan. The others: Rhizobium – a bacterium; yeast – a fungus; mushroom – a fungus.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Algae are grouped with plant-like microbes.
Reason (R): Algae contain chlorophyll and make their own food.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a virus?
items.answer: Penicillium
items.markingKey: (c) Penicillium is a fungus, not a virus. Each of the others (the polio virus, the common cold virus, the measles virus) is a virus.

items.stem: Classify these microorganisms as a protozoan or a virus: Amoeba, the polio virus, Euglena, the influenza virus, the common cold virus, Paramecium.
items.answer: A protozoan: Amoeba, Euglena, Paramecium. A virus: the common cold virus, the influenza virus, the polio virus.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A protozoan: Amoeba, Euglena, Paramecium. A virus: the common cold virus, the influenza virus, the polio virus.

items.stem: A bacterium divides into two every 30 minutes under ideal conditions. If 2 bacteria are present at the start, how many will there be after 3 hours?
items.markingKey: Number of divisions = 180 ÷ 30 = 6; number = 2 × 2^6 = 128.

items.stem:
Read: Students left three dishes open in the school lab for 30 minutes: one with boiled potato slice, one with moist bread, and one with dry rice. After four days in a warm cupboard, fuzzy coloured patches appeared on the potato and bread, but not on the rice.
(i) What are the fuzzy patches? (ii) Where did they come from? (iii) Why did the dry rice not show them? (iv) Suggest one safety precaution while observing them.
items.answer: (i) Colonies of moulds (fungi) and bacteria. (ii) Spores and microbes present in the air. (iii) Microbes need moisture to grow. (iv) Do not open the covered dish or smell it; wash hands; dispose of it safely.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem:
Read: Imran studied the growth of bacteria in a nutrient broth at 30 °C. The count was 20 at the start, 40 after 30 min, 80 after 60 min and 160 after 90 min.
(i) How long do the bacteria take to double? (ii) Predict the count after 120 min. (iii) Would growth be faster or slower at 37 °C (warm room)? (iv) Use this to explain why cooked food should be refrigerated.
items.answer: (i) 30 min. (ii) 320. (iii) Faster (near body temperature). (iv) Cold slows bacterial multiplication, so food stays safe longer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A microbe that can reproduce only inside the cells of a living host."
items.answer: a virus
items.markingKey: (b) A virus is a microbe that can reproduce only inside the cells of a living host.

items.stem: A bacterium divides into two every 15 minutes under ideal conditions. If 10 bacteria are present at the start, how many will there be after 3 hours?
items.markingKey: Number of divisions = 180 ÷ 15 = 12; number = 10 × 2^12 = 40960.

items.stem: A single bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes. Explain why food left out at room temperature for a few hours can become unsafe, even if it was clean at first.
items.answer: In 3 hours there are 9 doublings, so one bacterium becomes 2⁹ = 512; a few bacteria become thousands, enough to spoil food or cause illness.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: doubling idea. 1 mark: number grows rapidly (e.g. 512 from one). 1 mark: link to spoilage/food poisoning.

items.stem: Which microorganism is responsible for making vaccines?
items.answer: weakened or killed microbes
items.markingKey: (a) Weakened or killed microbes is responsible for making vaccines.

items.stem: Which of these is a use of yeast?
items.answer: making bread and idli batter rise
items.markingKey: (a) Yeast: making bread and idli batter rise.
options: making bread and idli batter rise
breaking down dead plants and animals into manure

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Bread is soft and spongy.
Reason (R): Carbon dioxide released by yeast during fermentation fills the dough.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A farmer plans to grow wheat after harvesting a crop of moong. Explain why his wheat crop may need less urea.
items.answer: Rhizobium in the root nodules of moong fixed atmospheric nitrogen into the soil, so some nitrogen is already available for wheat.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Rhizobium/nitrogen. 1 mark: soil enriched.

items.stem: Which of these would be the best place to keep a compost pit for a school garden: a sunny dry corner, a shady moist corner, or a concrete-lined tank with no holes? Explain.
items.answer: A shady, moist corner with soil contact: decomposers need moisture and moderate temperature and access to soil organisms; a sealed tank lacks air and drainage.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: choice. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem:
Read: Harleen's mother mixed sugar and a little yeast in warm water, then added flour to make dough. After two hours in a warm place, the dough had doubled in size. Another batch made with very hot water did not rise.
(i) Why did the first dough rise? (ii) Name this process. (iii) Why did the second batch not rise? (iv) What is the role of sugar?
items.answer: (i) Yeast released carbon dioxide which got trapped in the dough. (ii) Fermentation. (iii) Very hot water killed the yeast. (iv) Sugar is food for yeast.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of these is a use of weakened or killed microbes?
items.answer: making vaccines
items.markingKey: (b) Weakened or killed microbes: making vaccines.
options: fixing nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The breaking down of dead plants and animals into simple substances by microbes."
items.answer: decomposition
items.markingKey: (c) Decomposition is the breaking down of dead plants and animals into simple substances by microbes.

items.stem: Pasteurised milk is heated to about:
items.answer: 70 °C for 15–30 seconds and then chilled quickly
items.markingKey: (c) 70 °C for 15–30 seconds and then chilled quickly.
options: 70 °C for 15–30 seconds and then chilled quickly

items.stem: Which method of preservation is commonly used for dry fruits and chips?
items.answer: airtight packing
items.markingKey: (c) Airtight packing: keeps out air, moisture and microbes.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): All microorganisms are harmful.
Reason (R): Some microorganisms cause diseases.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false: many are useful; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Classify these diseases by the microbe that causes them — protozoa or viruses: (1) yellow vein mosaic of bhindi; (2) common cold; (3) amoebic dysentery; (4) malaria; (5) chickenpox.
items.answer: Protozoa: amoebic dysentery; malaria. Viruses: chickenpox; common cold; yellow vein mosaic of bhindi.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Protozoa: amoebic dysentery; malaria. Viruses: chickenpox; common cold; yellow vein mosaic of bhindi.

items.stem: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by viruses?
items.answer: anthrax
items.markingKey: (d) Anthrax is caused by bacteria, not viruses. Each of the others (yellow vein mosaic of bhindi, measles, chickenpox) is caused by viruses.

items.stem:
Read: After a wedding feast in Patna, several guests fell ill with vomiting and stomach pain. The leftover rice and paneer curry had been kept uncovered at room temperature for about 10 hours before being served again.
(i) Name the illness. (ii) What caused it? (iii) Give two ways in which the food could have been kept safe. (iv) Why should one not taste food to check whether it is spoilt?
items.answer: (i) Food poisoning. (ii) Microbes grew in the food and produced toxins. (iii) Refrigerate within two hours; cover the food; reheat thoroughly. (iv) Toxins can be harmful even in small amounts and may not change the taste.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each (iii: any two).

items.stem: Explain why the leaves of bhindi plants in a farm turned yellow with green veins, and why spraying an antibiotic did not help.
items.answer: Yellow vein mosaic is caused by a virus (spread by whiteflies); antibiotics act only on bacteria, so they have no effect on viruses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: viral disease. 1 mark: antibiotics do not act on viruses.

items.stem: Which method of preservation is commonly used for squashes and jams (sodium benzoate, sodium metabisulphite)?
items.answer: adding chemical preservatives
items.markingKey: (d) Adding chemical preservatives: the chemicals check the growth of microbes.

items.stem: How does drying help to preserve food? Name one food preserved this way.
items.answer: Microbes need moisture to grow. Example: papad, raisins and red chillies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: how microbial growth is checked. 1 mark: example.

items.stem: Why are cheek cells collected by gently scraping the inner side of the cheek with a clean toothpick or spoon?
items.answer: The inner lining of the cheek sheds cells easily; gentle scraping collects them without injury, and clean tools avoid contamination.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cells come off easily. 1 mark: hygiene/no injury.

items.stem: Which part of the cell controls all its activities?
items.answer: Nucleus
items.markingKey: (a) Nucleus.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a protozoan?
items.answer: diatoms
items.markingKey: (c) Diatoms is an alga, not a protozoan. Each of the others (Euglena, Amoeba, Plasmodium) is a protozoan.

items.stem: Why does idli or dosa batter rise and smell sour when left overnight?
items.answer: Microbes (yeast and bacteria) ferment the batter, producing carbon dioxide, which makes it rise, and acids, which make it sour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: fermentation by microbes. 1 mark: CO₂ rises, acid sours.

items.stem: Explain why a few spoons of yeast can raise a large amount of dough, but the dough stops rising if it is left in a refrigerator.
items.answer: Yeast cells multiply in the warm dough and each produces carbon dioxide, so a little yeast becomes a large population. In the cold, yeast activity slows down, so little gas is made.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: multiplication. 1 mark: CO₂. 1 mark: low temperature slows yeast.

items.stem: Classify these diseases by the microbe that causes them — protozoa or viruses: (1) amoebic dysentery; (2) yellow vein mosaic of bhindi; (3) common cold; (4) chickenpox; (5) malaria.
items.answer: Protozoa: amoebic dysentery; malaria. Viruses: chickenpox; common cold; yellow vein mosaic of bhindi.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Protozoa: amoebic dysentery; malaria. Viruses: chickenpox; common cold; yellow vein mosaic of bhindi.

items.stem: Why do slices of bread left in a moist, warm place develop mould faster?
items.answer: Mould spores present in air need moisture, warmth and food to grow; these are available on moist bread.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: spores in air. 1 mark: moisture/warmth favour growth.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Green bodies in plant cells that contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis."
items.answer: chloroplasts
items.markingKey: (c) Chloroplasts is green bodies in plant cells that contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

items.stem: Classify the following into a unicellular organism and a multicellular organism: frog, Paramecium, grass, Euglena.
items.answer: A unicellular organism: Euglena, Paramecium. A multicellular organism: frog, grass.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A unicellular organism: Euglena, Paramecium. A multicellular organism: frog, grass.

items.stem: Why does stagnant water near houses increase cases of malaria and dengue?
items.answer: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water and spread the disease-causing microbes when they bite.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: breeding site. 1 mark: vector spreads disease.

items.stem: Under high power, Gauri sees only a blurred, very dark image of her cheek-cell slide. Give two possible reasons and the remedy for each.
items.answer: Too little light: open the diaphragm or adjust the mirror. Not focused: use the fine adjustment knob. (Also: specimen too thick—make a thinner smear.)
items.markingKey: 1 mark per reason with remedy (any two).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a virus?
items.answer: bread mould (Rhizopus)
items.markingKey: (c) Bread mould (Rhizopus) is a fungus, not a virus. Each of the others (the influenza virus, the polio virus, the measles virus) is a virus.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The total magnification of a microscope is the sum of eyepiece and objective magnifications.
Reason (R): The objective forms a magnified image that the eyepiece magnifies again.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false: magnifications multiply; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define an antibiotic.
items.answer: A medicine made from microorganisms that kills or stops the growth of bacteria
items.markingKey: 1 mark: An antibiotic – a medicine made from microorganisms that kills or stops the growth of bacteria.

items.stem: A bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes under ideal conditions. If 100 bacteria are present at the start, how many will there be after 2 hours?
items.markingKey: Number of divisions = 120 ÷ 20 = 6; number = 100 × 2^6 = 6400.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a unicellular organism?
items.answer: earthworm
items.markingKey: (c) Earthworm is a multicellular organism, not a unicellular organism. Each of the others (Paramecium, Euglena, bacteria) is a unicellular organism.

items.stem: Which of the following is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
items.answer: cell wall
items.markingKey: (a) Cell wall is found in plant cells but not in animal cells. The others: nucleus – found in both plant and animal cells; cell membrane – found in both plant and animal cells; mitochondria – found in both plant and animal cells.

items.stem: Sahil uses a microscope with a 10× eyepiece and a 10× objective lens. What is the total magnification?
items.markingKey: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 10 × 10 = 100×.

items.stem: What is meant by a colony?
items.answer: A visible group of many microbes that have grown from one or a few cells
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A colony – a visible group of many microbes that have grown from one or a few cells.

items.stem: How does pasteurisation help to preserve food? Name one food preserved this way.
items.answer: Milk is heated to about 70 °C for 15 to 30 seconds and suddenly chilled, which kills most microbes. Example: milk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: how microbial growth is checked. 1 mark: example.

items.stem: Why do we stain cells before observing them under a microscope?
items.answer: Most cell parts are colourless; stains colour parts such as the nucleus so they become clearly visible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: parts are transparent/colourless. 1 mark: stain makes nucleus/parts visible.

items.stem: A nerve cell is long and branched. This shape helps it to:
items.answer: carry messages over long distances
items.markingKey: (d) carry messages over long distances.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a bacterium?
items.answer: the measles virus
items.markingKey: (b) The measles virus is a virus, not a bacterium. Each of the others (the tuberculosis germ, Rhizobium, Lactobacillus) is a bacterium.

items.stem: Why do farmers grow legumes such as moong or gram between two cereal crops?
items.answer: Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes nitrogen and enriches the soil, so less fertiliser is needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Rhizobium/nitrogen fixation. 1 mark: soil fertility restored.

items.stem: A farmer grows wheat every year in the same field and finds the yield falling. Suggest how microorganisms can help him without buying more urea, and explain why.
items.answer: Grow a legume crop such as gram or moong between wheat crops (crop rotation); Rhizobium in root nodules fixes nitrogen and restores soil fertility. He can also add compost made by decomposers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: legume/crop rotation. 1 mark: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen. 1 mark: compost/other microbial method.

items.stem: Classify these diseases by the microbe that causes them — protozoa or fungi: ringworm, amoebic dysentery, malaria, rust of wheat.
items.answer: Protozoa: amoebic dysentery, malaria. Fungi: ringworm, rust of wheat.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Protozoa: amoebic dysentery, malaria. Fungi: ringworm, rust of wheat.

items.stem: Why are microorganisms found almost everywhere, even in hot springs and icy regions?
items.answer: They are very small, multiply rapidly and many kinds can survive extreme conditions, some forming protective spores.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: small size and rapid multiplication. 1 mark: tolerance/spores.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A space in the cytoplasm filled with cell sap; it is large in plant cells."
items.answer: a vacuole
items.markingKey: (d) A vacuole is a space in the cytoplasm filled with cell sap; it is large in plant cells.

items.stem: Classify the following into a multicellular organism and a unicellular organism: grass, earthworm, bacteria, yeast, mushroom.
items.answer: A multicellular organism: earthworm, grass, mushroom. A unicellular organism: bacteria, yeast.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A multicellular organism: earthworm, grass, mushroom. A unicellular organism: bacteria, yeast.

items.stem: Why do pickles last for months without spoiling?
items.answer: The salt, oil and acid (vinegar or lemon) in pickles do not allow microbes to grow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: salt/oil/acid named. 1 mark: microbes cannot grow.

items.stem: Yash sees only a dark circle with a thick black rim at the centre of his onion-peel slide, and no cells. Suggest what went wrong and how to correct it.
items.answer: An air bubble was trapped under the coverslip. Lower the coverslip gently at an angle using a needle so that air is pushed out.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: air bubble identified. 1 mark: correct method.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a fungus?
items.answer: the tuberculosis germ
items.markingKey: (a) The tuberculosis germ is a bacterium, not a fungus. Each of the others (mushroom, yeast, Penicillium) is a fungus.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A thin peel of onion is used to make a slide.
Reason (R): Light must pass through the specimen for it to be seen under a microscope.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by fermentation?
items.answer: The conversion of sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide (or acids) by microorganisms such as yeast
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Fermentation – the conversion of sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide (or acids) by microorganisms such as yeast.

items.stem: A bacterium divides into two every 30 minutes under ideal conditions. If 10 bacteria are present at the start, how many will there be after 1 hour?
items.markingKey: Number of divisions = 60 ÷ 30 = 2; number = 10 × 2^2 = 40.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a multicellular organism?
items.answer: Paramecium
items.markingKey: (d) Paramecium is a unicellular organism, not a multicellular organism. Each of the others (human being, earthworm, grass) is a multicellular organism.

items.stem: Which of the following is found in both plant and animal cells?
items.answer: cell membrane
items.markingKey: (a) Cell membrane is found in both plant and animal cells. The others: a large central vacuole – found in plant cells but not in animal cells; chloroplasts – found in plant cells but not in animal cells; cell wall – found in plant cells but not in animal cells.

items.stem: Varun uses a microscope with a 10× eyepiece and a 4× objective lens. What is the total magnification?
items.markingKey: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 10 × 4 = 40×.

items.stem: Define a protozoan.
items.answer: A single-celled, animal-like microorganism such as Amoeba or Paramecium
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A protozoan – a single-celled, animal-like microorganism such as Amoeba or Paramecium.
